counties: [4 Mar 1628/1629] King Charles I chartered Mass. Bay Co. to establish a colony stretching from 3 mi. N of the Merrimack R., to 3 mi. S of the Charles R. & extending from the Atlantic to the Pacific. N limit in dispute, only mod. limits of MA mapped.

[13 Jan 1629/1630] The Council for New England issued a new land patent (the "Old Charter") that granted land title and trading rights, but no powers of government, to New Plymouth colony. New Plymouth Colony included part of present Rhode Island.
[1634] CHARLES CITY created as one of the eight original shires.
[1634] ELIZABETH CITY (extinct) created as one of the eight original shires.
[1634] HENRICO created as one of the eight original shires.
[1634] WARROSQUYOAKE (renamed ISLE OF WIGHT in 1637) created as one of the eight original shires.
[1634] JAMES CITY created as one of the eight original shires.
[1634] ACCOMACK (original, renamed NORTHAMPTON in 1643) created as one of the eight original shires.
[1634] WARWICK RIVER (renamed WARWICK in 1643, extinct) created as one of the eight original shires.
[1634] CHARLES RIVER (renamed YORK in 1643) created as one of the eight original shires.
[1636] ELIZABETH CITY (extinct) lost to creation of NEW NORFOLK (extinct).
[1636] NEW NORFOLK (extinct) created from ELIZABETH CITY (extinct).
[1637] WARROSQUYOAKE renamed ISLE OF WIGHT [no mappable change].
[1637] LOWER NORFOLK (extinct) created from NEW NORFOLK; NEW NORFOLK County eliminated.
[1637] UPPER NORFOLK (later NANSEMOND, extinct) created from NEW NORFOLK; NEW NORFOLK County eliminated.
Non-County Area 1 created from all that part of present Maryland outside of ST. MARYS.
By 24 January 1637/1638, ST. MARYS was created as the first county in Maryland. ST. MARYS was meant to serve the entire colony; territorial limits, if any, are unknown, and boundaries are estimated.
By 2 August 1642, KENT was created from ST. MARYS to serve the east side of Chesapeake Bay; territorial limits were not specified, and boundaries are estimated.
By 2 August 1642, ST. MARYS lost to creation of KENT; boundaries are estimated.
In 1642, Massachusetts, responding to a request from disgruntled Rhode Islanders, extended its jurisdiction over the settlement at Pawtuxet.
[1642] UPPER NORFOLK renamed NANSEMOND (extinct) [no mappable change].
ESSEX created as one of four original counties in Massachusetts.
MIDDLESEX created as one of four original counties in Massachusetts.
Non-County Area 1 in Massachusetts colony was unsettled, unorganized area covering the western half of the province.
NORFOLK (original, extinct) created as one of four original Massachusetts counties; included New Hampshire settlements.
SUFFOLK created as one of four original counties in Massachusetts. SUFFOLK included territory in the northeast corner of present Rhode Island.
[1643] WARWICK RIVER renamed WARWICK (extinct) [no mappable change].
[1643] CHARLES RIVER renamed YORK [no mappable change].
[14 March 1643/1644] Roger Williams secured a Parliamentary patent for Rhode Island (called "Providence Plantations") that granted authority for self-government; western boundary is estimated.
[1648] YORK lost to creation of NORTHUMBERLAND.
ANNE ARUNDEL created from ST. MARYS. The county was centered on the settlement of Providence, but territorial limits were not otherwise specified.
ST. MARYS lost to creation of ANNE ARUNDEL.
CHARLES (original, extinct) created from ST. MARYS; boundaries are estimated.
ST. MARYS lost to creation of CHARLES (original, extinct).
[1651] LANCASTER created from both NORTHUMBERLAND and YORK.
[1651] NORTHUMBERLAND lost to creation of LANCASTER.
[1651] YORK lost to creation of both GLOUCESTER and LANCASTER.

Massachusetts created YORKSHIRE (now YORK) in Maine after southern Maine towns acknowledged Mass. jurisdiction to territory within the new boundaries it declared on 26 May 1652. Claim conflicted with 1635 grant of Maine to Ferdinando Gorges.
[1652] JAMES CITY lost to creation of SURRY.
[1653] NORTHUMBERLAND lost to creation of WESTMORELAND.
ANNE ARUNDEL lost to creation of CALVERT; boundaries are estimated.
CALVERT created from ANNE ARUNDEL and CHARLES (original, extinct); CHARLES (original) eliminated. CALVERT boundaries are estimated.
ANNE ARUNDEL renamed PROVIDENCE; PROVIDENCE gained from PATUXENT (now CALVERT).
CALVERT renamed PATUXENT; PATUXENT lost to PROVIDENCE (now ANNE ARUNDEL).
[1654] YORK lost to creation of NEW KENT.
LANCASTER lost to creation of RAPPAHANNOCK (original, extinct).
[1656] ISLE OF WIGHT gained from NANSEMOND (extinct).
[1656] NANSEMOND (extinct) lost to ISLE OF WIGHT.
CHARLES created from ST. MARYS; territorial limits not specified, and boundaries are estimated.
ST. MARYS lost to creation of CHARLES.
The Pawtuxet settlers, who gave their allegiance to Massachusetts in 1642, returned to Rhode Island jurisdiction.
By 12 January 1659/1660, ANNE ARUNDEL lost to creation of BALTIMORE.

By 12 January 1659/1660, BALTIMORE was created from ANNE ARUNDEL, KENT, and Non-County Area 1 between ANNE ARUNDEL and KENT. BALTIMORE territorial limits, if any, are unknown and boundaries are estimated.
By 12 January 1659/1660, KENT lost to creation of BALTIMORE.
Non-County Area 1 lost to creation of BALTIMORE and Non-County Area 2.
Non-County Area 2 created from Non-County Area 1.
By 18 February 1661/1662, KENT lost to creation of TALBOT.
Non-County Area 2 lost to creation of TALBOT.
By 18 February 1661/1662, TALBOT was created from KENT and Non-County Area 2; TALBOT territorial limits, if any, are unknown, and boundaries are estimated.

King Charles II granted Connecticut a charter as a self-governing corporate colony with an eastern boundary at Narragansett Bay. R.I. did not concede its claim to area between the Pawcatuck R. and Narragansett Bay, but Conn. took control of the area.
HAMPSHIRE created from Non-County Area 1 (towns of Springfield, Northampton, Hadley, and all territory within 30 miles), effectively covering entire western part of the province.
New Plymouth Colony lost to Rhode Island when King Charles II granted Rhode Island a charter as a self-governing corporate colony.
SUFFOLK lost to Rhode Island when the provincial boundary was adjusted after King Charles II granted Rhode Island a charter as a self-governing corporate colony.

King Charles II granted Rhode Island a charter as a self-governing corporate colony. The charter's boundary descriptions included Narragansett Country, and also resulted in gains from New Plymouth (in Narragansett Bay), and from SUFFOLK (Mass.).
[1663] NORTHAMPTON lost to creation of ACCOMACK.
[May 1664] New Plymouth Colony gained from SUFFOLK and Rhode Island Colony when a joint commission from Massachusetts and Plymouth demarcated their mutual boundary ("Old Colony Line").
[May 1664] SUFFOLK lost to the New Plymouth Colony when a joint commission from Massachusetts and Plymouth demarcated their mutual boundary ("Old Colony Line").
[May 1664] Rhode Island lost the northeast corner of the present state to New Plymouth when a joint commission from Massachusetts and Plymouth demarcated their mutual boundary ("Old Colony Line").
[Nov. 1664] Representatives of the Gorges family rejected Massachusetts's claim and resumed government of Maine (area between the Kennebec and Piscataqua Rivers). YORKSHIRE went into abeyance.
[1664] WESTMORELAND lost to creation of STAFFORD.
[7 Jan 1664/1665] ALBEMARLE (extinct) created as one of three original counties (the only one in present North Carolina) by the Carolina Lords Proprietors; boundary limits were indefinite.

[27 February 1664/1665] New Plymouth gained from Rhode Island Colony when royal boundary commissioners set Rhode Island's eastern limit along the Blackstone River and east coast of Narragansett Bay, pending a conclusive royal decision.

[27 Feb 1664/1665] SUFFOLK gained from Rhode Island Colony when royal commissioners set the provincial boundaries of Mass., New Plymouth, and R.I. along the Blackstone River and the east side of Narragansett Bay, pending conclusive royal decision.

[27 February 1664/1665] Rhode Island Colony lost to SUFFOLK (Mass.) and to New Plymouth Colony when royal boundary commissioners set eastern boundary of R.I. along Blackstone River and east side of Narragansett Bay, pending a conclusive royal decision.

Royal commissioners decided dispute over the Narragansett Country by dismissing Mass. claim, putting Conn. claim in abeyance, and giving R. I. temp. authority. Conn. claim to area not abandoned until boundary settlement of 12 May 1703.

King's Province established by royal commissioners who decided dispute over the Narragansett Country by dismissing Mass. claim, putting Conn. claim in abeyance, and placing area under royal jurisdiction. R. I. given temp. authority over Kings Province.

Royal commissioners decided dispute over the Narragansett Country by placing it directly under royal jurisdiction. Named King's Province; R.I. given temp. authority pending royal decision. King's Province treated here as separate from Rhode Island.
Royal commissioners replaced Gorges's jurisdiction over Maine (between Piscataqua and Kennebec Rivers) with a new government under direct authority of the crown.

CORNWALL (extinct) created by New York to cover all of the Duke of York's grant between the Kennebec and St. Croix Rivers in present Maine and Quebec, Canada. CORNWALL eliminated in 1675 when war broke out between the Abnaki Indians and the English.
FAIRFIELD created by the Colony of Connecticut as one of four original counties; part of its western limit was not clearly defined, but included part of New York (town of Rye).
HARTFORD created by the Colony of Connecticut as one of four original counties.
Non-County Area 1 created when the Colony of Connecticut created four original counties.
Non-County Area 2 created when the Colony of Connecticut created four original counties.
NEW HAVEN created by the Colony of Connecticut as one of four original counties.
NEW LONDON created by Colony of Connecticut as one of four original counties.
Non-County Area 2 lost to creation of SOMERSET.

SOMERSET created from Non-County Area 2 south of TALBOT. Area included all land between the Nanticoke River and the Atlantic Ocean (including part of southern Delaware), but Maryland did not try to exercise jurisdiction in the eastern part.
Massachusetts reasserted authority over all of Maine west of the Kennebec R., an area that had been put under royal government in June 1665.
YORK (formerly called YORKSHIRE) reinstated when Massachusetts reasserted authority over all of Maine west of the Kennebec River, an area that had been put under royal government in June 1665.
By 16 February 1668/1669, DORCHESTER was created from Non-County Area 2 between SOMERSET and TALBOT. DORCHESTER territorial limits, if any, are unknown; boundaries were partially defined 6 May 1669.

Non-County Area 2 lost to HAMPSHIRE (Mass.) when town of Westfield (now Southwick, Mass.) was created from town of Springfield. Part of Westfield extended into Conn., the result of disagreement over the line between Conn. and Mass.

HAMPSHIRE gained from non-county area in Connecticut when the town of Westfield (now Southwick) was created from the town of Springfield. Part of Westfield extended into Connecticut, the result of disagreement over the line between the two colonies.

Maryland implicitly claimed part of present Delaware and Pennsylvania (then controlled by New York) by creating DURHAM (extinct) from SOMERSET and non-county area along the Atlantic Coast. DURHAM was never operational.
Non-County Area 3 created from SOMERSET when SOMERSET lost to creation of an unnamed county in Maryland and present southern Delaware, which never became operational.
SOMERSET lost to creation of an unnamed county located in Maryland and present southern Delaware, and to creation of DURHAM (extinct). These counties never became operational.
HARTFORD gained town of Simsbury from Non-County Area 2.
Non-County Area 2 lost town of Simsbury to HARTFORD, and lost to creation of Non-County Area 3.
Non-County Area 3 created from Non-County Area 2.
Non-County Area 2 lost town of Wallingford to NEW HAVEN, and lost to creation of Non-County Area 4.
Non-County Area 4 created from Non-County Area 2.
NEW HAVEN gained town of Wallingford from Non-County Area 2.
KENT gained from TALBOT; boundaries are estimated.
TALBOT lost to KENT; boundaries are estimated.
[c. 1671] Carteret Precinct (original, extinct) created in ALBEMARLE; southern boundary limit, below Albermarle Sound, was indefinite.
[c. 1671] Shaftesbury Precinct (now CHOWAN) created in ALBEMARLE; southern and western boundary limits were indefinite.
[c. 1671] Berkeley Precinct (now PERQUIMANS) created in ALBEMARLE; southern boundary limit, below Albermarle Sound, was indefinite.

WORCESTER (original, extinct) created from DURHAM (extinct) and the unnamed coastal county in present Maryland and Delaware. WORCESTER (original) was located in present Delaware and Pennsylvania and never became operational.

After completing their re-conquest of New York in August 1673, the Dutch created NEW AMSTEL (now NEW CASTLE) in present Delaware [no inland limits were specified]. NEW AMSTEL became dependent on New York in 1674.

After completing their re-conquest of New York in August 1673, the Dutch created HOARKILL (later DEALE, now SUSSEX) as one of three county-like courts that became original counties in Delaware; no inland limits were specified.

After completing their re-conquest of New York in August 1673, the Dutch created UPLAND (extinct) in present Delaware and Pennsylvania [no inland limit was specified]. UPLAND became dependent on New York in 1674.
By 7 October 1673, Massachusetts claimed some of the Duke of York's territory in present Maine and created DEVONSHIRE (extinct). County was unnamed until 27 May 1674.

Non-County Area 3 lost to HAMPSHIRE (Mass.) when town of Suffield created. Suffield was entirely within present Conn., the result of uncertain geographic knowledge and disagreement over the boundary between the colonies.

HAMPSHIRE gained non-county area in Connecticut when the town of Suffield was created. Suffield was entirely within present Connecticut, the result of uncertain geographical knowledge and disagreement over the boundary between the colonies.
ANNE ARUNDEL gained from CALVERT and Non-County Area 1.
By 6 June 1674, BALTIMORE lost to creation of CECIL.
By 6 June 1674, CECIL was created from BALTIMORE and KENT.
By 6 June 1674, KENT lost to creation of CECIL.
Non-County Area 1 lost to ANNE ARUNDEL.
CECIL lost to KENT; boundary is estimated.
KENT gained from CECIL; boundary is estimated.
By 11 Nov 1674 NEW AMSTEL was renamed NEW CASTLE.
[1674] LANCASTER lost to creation of MIDDLESEX.
Non-County Area 2 lost town of Derby to NEW HAVEN.
NEW HAVEN gained town of Derby from Non-County Area 2.
FAIRFIELD gained town of Woodbury from Non-County Area 2.
Non-County Area 2 lost town of Woodbury to FAIRFIELD.

George Carteret and the other New Jersey proprietors executed the Quintipartite Deed to divide New Jersey into two distinct colonies, East New Jersey and West New Jersey. Both colonies were unorganized and technically were non-county areas.

George Carteret and the other New Jersey proprietors executed the Quintipartite Deed to divide New Jersey into two distinct colonies, East New Jersey and West New Jersey. Both colonies were unorganized and technically were non-county areas.
ESSEX gained towns of Amesbury, Haverhill, and Salisbury from NORFOLK (original) when King Charles II made New Hampshire a royal colony separate from Massachusetts; NORFOLK (original) eliminated.
King Charles II made New Hampshire a royal colony separate from Massachusetts; no western limit was specified. See Consolidated Chronology for changes in the status of New Hampshire to 1769.

[17 Mar 1679/1680] YORK (Me.) eliminated when Massachusetts organized a new government for Maine (area between the Piscataqua and Kennebec Rivers) in accordance with terms of Ferdinando Gorges's 1635 grant.
ST. JONES (now KENT) created under the authority of the Duke of York from NEW CASTLE and HOARKILL (later DEALE, now SUSSEX); no inland limits specified.
NEW CASTLE lost to creation of ST. JONES (now KENT).
HOARKILL (later DEALE, now SUSSEX) lost to creation of ST. JONES (now KENT); no inland limits specified.
King Charles II created Pennsylvania from parts of earlier grants to Connecticut and Virginia, granting it as a proprietary colony to William Penn.
By 15 June 1681, HOARKILL renamed DEALE (now SUSSEX).
The Indefinite Counties Area implicitly arose when West New Jersey created Burlington and Salem courts without definite boundaries. The northern limit along the Assunpink Creek is estimated.
The creation of the county-like courts of Burlington and Salem in the southern portion of West New Jersey left the northern portion of the colony completely unorganized as a non-county area.
BERKELEY (original, extinct) created as one of three original counties [inland boundary extent is estimated line].
COLLETON (original, extinct) created as one of three original counties [inland boundary extent is estimated line].
CRAVEN (extinct) created as one of three original counties [inland boundary extent is estimated line].
ST. JONES (now KENT) was transferred with the rest of the western Delaware Bay region from the Duke of York to William Penn.
NEW CASTLE transferred with rest of western Delaware Bay region from the Duke of York to William Penn; implicitly gained the southern tip of UPLAND remaining after county was eliminated in Jun 1681.
DEALE (now SUSSEX) was transferred with the rest of the western Delaware Bay region from the Duke of York to William Penn.
By 21 December 1682, ST. JONES renamed KENT.
DEALE renamed SUSSEX; SUSSEX gained from KENT.
7 March 1682/1683. BERGEN created as one of four original counties in East New Jersey.
7 March 1682/1683. ESSEX created as one of four original counties in East New Jersey. Two segments of line between ESSEX and West New Jersey are estimated. NCA (East) eliminated.
7 March 1682/1683. MIDDLESEX created as one of four original counties in East New Jersey.
7 March 1682/1683. MONMOUTH created as one of four original counties in East New Jersey.

HAMPSHIRE gained non-county area in Connecticut when town of Enfield was created. Most of Enfield was in present Connecticut, the result of uncertain geographical knowledge and disagreement over the boundary between the colonies.
ALBANY created from non-county area in New York; northern limit was not defined.
New York re-created CORNWALL (extinct) to cover all of the Duke of York's grant in present Maine and Quebec, including the Pemaquid settlement governed since 1674 by Massachusetts.
DUKES (extinct) created to cover the 1674 grant to the Duke of York of islands in Massachusetts, including Martha's Vineyard, Nantucket, and Elizabeth Islands.
DUTCHESS created from non-county area in New York.
KINGS created from the shire of Yorkshire, which had been organized in 1664.
Non-County Area 1 (Brothers Islands and Hulett's [now Rikers] Island) created from Yorkshire.
Non-County Area 2 (the Oyster Islands [now Ellis, Liberty, and Governors Islands]) created from Yorkshire.
Non-County Area 3 (City I., Hart I., Manursing I., and other small islands in Long Island Sound) created from Yorkshire.
NEW YORK created from Yorkshire, which had been organized in New York in 1664.
ORANGE created from non-county area in New York.
QUEENS created from Yorkshire, which had been organized in 1664.
RICHMOND created from Yorkshire, which had been organized in New York in 1664.
SUFFOLK created from Yorkshire, which had been organized in New York in 1664.
ULSTER created from non-county area in New York.
WESTCHESTER created from Yorkshire, which had been organized in 1664.
FAIRFIELD lost to WESTCHESTER (N.Y.) when the provincial boundary between Connecticut and New York was adjusted and the town of Rye reverted to New York.
Non-County Area 3 gained additional small islands in Long Island Sound when Fairfield (Conn.) eliminated from New York.
WESTCHESTER gained from FAIRFIELD (Conn.) when the provincial boundary between Connecticut and New York was adjusted.
[c. 1684] Currituck Precinct (now CURRITUCK) created from Carteret Precinct (original), extinct in ALBEMARLE; Carteret Precinct eliminated.
[c. 1684] Pasquotank Precinct (now PASQUOTANK) created from Carteret Precinct (original, extinct) in ALBEMARLE; Carteret Precinct eliminated.
[12 Mar 1684/1685] BERKELEY (original, extinct) gained from CRAVEN and unorganized territory, exchanged with COLLETON [inland boundary extent is estimated line].
[12 Mar 1684/1685] COLLETON (extinct) gained from unorganized territory, exchanged with BERKELEY (original, extinct) [inland boundary extent is estimated line].
[12 Mar 1684/1685] CRAVEN (extinct) gained from unorganized territory, lost to BERKELEY (original, extinct) [inland boundary extent is estimated line].
[12 Mar 1684/1685] GRANVILLE (original, extinct) created from unorganized territory [inland boundary extent is estimated line].
BUCKS created as one of three original counties in Pennsylvania in 1682 but no boundaries were specified. On 1 Apr 1685 BUCKS boundaries defined.
CHESTER created as one of three original counties in Pennsylvania in 1682 but no boundaries were specified. On 1 Apr 1685 CHESTER boundaries defined.
Non-County Area 1 created from that part of the colony of Pennsylvania outside the three original counties.
PHILADELPHIA created as one of three original counties in Pennsylvania in 1682 but no boundaries were specified. On 1 Apr 1685 PHILADELPHIA boundaries defined.
BARNSTABLE created as one of three original counties in New Plymouth Colony.
BRISTOL created as one of three original counties in New Plymouth Colony.
PLYMOUTH created as one of three original counties in New Plymouth Colony.
SUSSEX by default implicitly gained remaining territory north of Maryland when King James II decided the area of Delaware did not belong to Maryland; boundary settled in 1760.

SOMERSET implicitly regained area along the Atlantic coast between Delaware and Virginia and lost northeastern tip in present Delaware when King James II decided the area of Delaware did not belong to Maryland.
HARTFORD gained town of Waterbury from Non-County Area 2.
Non-County Area 2 lost town of Waterbury to HARTFORD.
8 January 1686/1687. ESSEX gained from non-county area in West New Jersey when the absentee governors of East and West New Jersey agreed on a new division between their colonies.
8 Jan 1687/1688. The Indefinite Counties Area lost to MIDDLESEX and MONMOUTH when the absentee governors of East and West New Jersey agree on a new division between their colonies.
8 January 1686/1687. MIDDLESEX gained from non-county area in West New Jersey when the absentee governors of East and West New Jersey agreed on a new division between their colonies.
8 January 1686/1687. MONMOUTH gained from non-county area in West New Jersey when the absentee governors of East and West New Jersey agreed on a new division between their colonies.
8 January 1686/1687. Non-County Area of West New Jersey lost to ESSEX, MIDDLESEX and MONMOUTH when the absentee governors of East and West New Jersey agreed on a new division between their colonies.
KENT gained from SUSSEX; lost to NEW CASTLE.
FAIRFIELD gained town of Danbury from Non-County Area 2.
Non-County Area 1 lost town of Preston to NEW LONDON.
Non-County Area 2 lost town of Danbury to FAIRFIELD.
NEW LONDON gained the town of Preston from Non-County Area 1.
MIDDLESEX lost to creation of SOMERSET.

ESSEX lost to West New Jersey when the absentee governors of East and West New Jersey agreed on a new partition line between their colonies that ran irregularly from the northern end of the Keith Line (1687) to the land boundary with New York.

The Non-County Area of West New Jersey gained from ESSEX and SOMERSET when the absentee governors of East and West New Jersey agreed on a compromise boundary between the two colonies from the north end of the Keith Line (1687) eastward to New York.

SOMERSET lost to West New Jersey when the absentee governors of East and West New Jersey agreed on a new partition line between their colonies that ran irregularly from the northern end of the Keith Line (1687) to the land boundary with New York.
[15 Mar 1689/1690] Non-County Area 1 lost to SUFFOLK (Mass.) when town of Woodstock created within present Connecticut.

[15 Mar 1689/1690] SUFFOLK gained non-county area in Conn. when Mass. created the town of Woodstock. Woodstock lay almost entirely within present Conn., the result of uncertain geographical knowledge and disagreement over the line bet. the two colonies.
KING AND QUEEN created from NEW KENT.
NEW KENT lost to creation of KING AND QUEEN.
NORFOLK (extinct) created from LOWER NORFOLK; LOWER NORFOLK eliminated.
PRINCESS ANNE (extinct) created from LOWER NORFOLK; LOWER NORFOLK eliminated.
DUTCHESS lost to creation of Non-County Area 4.
NEW YORK gained all of Non-County Area 2 (the Oyster Islands [now Ellis, Liberty, and Governors Islands]).
QUEENS gained all of Non-County Area 1 (the Brother Islands and Huletts [now Rikers] Island).

King William III & Queen Mary II issued a new charter for the province of Mass. Bay, extending boundaries to encompass New Plymouth Colony, Nantucket, Martha's Vineyard; and territory in present Maine. Map depicts non-county area in Mass. Bay Colony.
YORK reinstated under new Massachusetts charter issued by King William III and Queen Mary II for the province of Massachusetts Bay.
CRAVEN (extinct) gained from unorganized territory [inland boundary extent was indefinite].
ESSEX created from RAPPAHANOCK (original); RAPPAHANOCK (original) eliminated.
RICHMOND created from RAPPAHANOCK (original); RAPPAHANOCK (original) eliminated.
Within the Indefinite Counties Area, West New Jersey converted the court of Cape May Court to CAPE MAY County; boundary description of CAPE MAY was complete and mappable.
Indefinite Counties Area in West New Jersey lost to CAPE MAY after that court was converted to a county and the boundaries were defined completely and clearly.
HARTFORD gained town of Windham from Non-County Area 1.
Non-County Area 1 lost town of Windham to HARTFORD.

The Indefinite Counties Area gained from CAPE MAY when CAPE MAY lost to GLOUCESTER. The area's northern boundary along Assunpink Cr. became definite when the creek was specified as the boundary bet. BURLINGTON and the NCA (West).
Non-county area in Massachusetts Bay Colony lost to creation of DUKES, and NANTUCKET.
DUKES created from non-county area in Massachusetts Bay Colony (Martha's Vineyard and the Elizabeth Islands).
NANTUCKET created from non-county area in Massachusetts Bay Colony (Nantucket Island).
CALVERT lost to CHARLES and ST. MARYS, and lost to creation of PRINCE GEORGES.
CHARLES gained from CALVERT, lost to creation of PRINCE GEORGES.
Non-County Area 1 lost to creation of PRINCE GEORGES.
PRINCE GEORGES created from CALVERT, CHARLES, and Non-County Area 1.
BATH (extinct) created for the Pamlico Sound region.
Non-County Area 1 lost the Quinebaug River Valley to NEW LONDON, and lost to creation of Non-County Area 5.
Non-County Area 5 created from Non-County Area 1.
NEW LONDON gained the Quinebaug River Valley from Non-County Area 1.
Non-County Area 1 lost the town of Colchester to NEW LONDON.
NEW LONDON gained the town of Colchester from Non-County Area 1.
Non-County Area 1 lost the town of Lebanon to NEW LONDON.
NEW LONDON gained the town of Lebanon from Non-County Area 1.
KING AND QUEEN lost to creation of KING WILLIAM.
KING WILLIAM created from KING AND QUEEN.
CHARLES CITY lost to creation of PRINCE GEORGE.
PRINCE GEORGE created from CHARLES CITY.

Rhode Island and Conn. agreed on their mutual boundary substantially along the line established by colonial agents in 1662, described in R.I.'s 1663 charter and claimed since then by Rhode Island. This boundary became effective almost immediately.
RHODE ISLAND County (now NEWPORT) created as one of two original counties, consisting of Block Island and the islands in Narragansett Bay.
PROVIDENCE PLANTATIONS (now PROVIDENCE) created as one of two original counties, consisting of the mainland part of Rhode Island.
By 29 November 1704, KENT was separated from Pennsylvania when Delaware became a distinct colony.
By 29 November 1704, NEW CASTLE was separated from Pennsylvania when Delaware became a distinct colony.
By 29 November 1704, SUSSEX was separated from Pennsylvania when Delaware became a distinct colony.
Pamptecough Precinct (now BEAUFORT) created in BATH; northwestern boundary limit was indefinite.
Archdale Precinct (now CRAVEN) created in BATH; northwestern boundary limit was indefinite. BATH effectively eliminated as a unit of government.
Wickham Precinct (now HYDE) created in BATH; northern boundary limit was indefinite.
Non-County Area 2 lost town of New Milford to NEW HAVEN, and lost to creation of Non-County Area 6.
Non-County Area 6 created from Non-County Area 2.
NEW HAVEN gained town of New Milford from Non-County Area 2.
Christ Church Parish created in BERKELEY County (original, extinct).
St. Andrew Parish created in BERKELEY County (original, extinct) [inland boundary extent is estimated line].
St. Bartholomew Parish created in COLLETON County (original, extinct) [inland boundary extent is estimated line].
St. James-Goose Creek Parish created in BERKELEY County (original, extinct) [inland boundary extent is estimated line].
St. James-Santee Parish created in CRAVEN County (extinct) [inland boundary extent is estimated line].
St. John-Berkeley Parish created in BERKELEY County (original, extinct) [inland boundary extent is estimated line].
St. Paul Parish created in COLLETON County (original, extinct).
St. Philip Parish created in BERKELEY County (original, extinct).

St. Thomas / St. Dennis Parishes created in BERKELEY County (original, extinct). Created as separate parishes, the boundary separating St. Thomas from St. Dennis was never clearly defined and by 1720 they were functioning as a single parish.
DORCHESTER lost to creation of QUEEN ANNES.
KENT gained from CECIL, lost to creation of QUEEN ANNES.
QUEEN ANNES created from DORCHESTER, KENT, and TALBOT.
TALBOT lost to creation of QUEEN ANNES.
BARNSTABLE lost town of Rochester to PLYMOUTH.
PLYMOUTH gained the town of Rochester from BARNSTABLE.
HARTFORD gained town of Hebron from Non-County Area 1.
Non-County Area 1 lost town of Hebron to HARTFORD.
NEW HAVEN gained town of Durham from Non-County Area 4. Non-County Area 4 eliminated.
HARTFORD gained town of Colchester from NEW LONDON.
NEW LONDON lost the town of Colchester to HARTFORD.
FAIRFIELD gained town of Ridgefield from Non-County Area 2.
Non-County Area 2 lost town of Ridgefield to FAIRFIELD.
